title: Align embeddings & rerank endpoints: unified error semantics and cursor-based pagination
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: deliver a minimal compatibility layer so customers using older embeddings/rerank clients see identical paging and error behavior as the new unified API. Scope includes: canonicalizing error codes (mapping older numeric and vendor-specific codes to our documented set), defining and implementing cursor-based pagination semantics for both embeddings and rerank endpoints, and creating SDK shims that avoid breaking changes for common client patterns. Out of scope: changing model scoring behavior or vector normalization semantics beyond compatibility fixes. Success measured by: no increase in customer-facing errors after rollout, <1% change in average request latency for affected endpoints, and SDK adoption of the shim in >=3 top customers during rollout window.
acceptance_criteria: Error mapping table published and reviewed by Runtime and API teams (Confluence link in related_links)
Server-side compatibility layer implemented in gateway that maps legacy error codes to documented API errors
Cursor-based pagination RFC approved and implemented with backwards-compatible defaults (limit param, next_cursor token format, and stable ordering defined)
SDK shims (Python and JS) released that translate legacy client calls to new pagination semantics without changing typical call patterns
Integration tests covering 100% of mapped error cases and pagination edge cases added to infra test suite
Rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback in case of >2% error uplift prepared and scheduled
notes: Decision: prefer opaque cursor tokens (base64-encoded state) over numeric offsets to preserve stable ordering when rerank changes internal sort keys
Trade-off: opaque cursors add server-side state decoding cost; mitigated by keeping cursor payload small and versioned
Compatibility approach: gateway shim only (no model/recompute changes) to minimize risk for Dedicated/Private customers
We will not expose internal KV-cache pointers in cursors to avoid leaking infra details
Edge case: when underlying index changes between pages, we will return an explicit pagination_invalidation error mapped to client-friendly code and include guidance to restart query
